Paragraph:
Translation: A person who has given up all desires for sense gratification, who lives free from desires, who has given up all sense of proprietorship and is devoid of false ego—he alone can attain real peace.

Purport (Excerpt): To become desireless means not to desire anything for sense gratification... To understand one's actual position as the eternal servitor of Krsna, without falsely claiming this material body to be oneself and without falsely claiming proprietorship... is the perfect stage...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The twin roots of all human psychological suffering: possessiveness ('mine') and false ego ('I').
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna defines the exact formula for ultimate peace (santim adhigacchati): 1) Giving up selfish desire, 2) Abandoning possessiveness (nirmama), and 3) Shedding false ego (nirahankara).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna receives the final behavioral profile required to live a completely liberated, unburdened life.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Ego Death / Dissolution: Living free from false identity and entitlement (nirahankara)
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Relinquishing Possessiveness: Releasing the toxic attachment of ownership (nirmama)
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Authentic Peace: The serene state achieved when selfish desires cease

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Desirelessness does not mean becoming an inactive stone; it means redirecting all desires toward divine service. When a person sheds the illusion that 'I am this body' (false ego) and 'This material world belongs to me' (possessiveness), they step into their true identity as a servant of God and experience absolute peace.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychological friction stems almost entirely from ego defense and possessiveness. When we tie our identity to titles, bodies, and possessions, we live in constant terror of loss. By practicing 'nirmama' (nothing is mine to possess) and 'nirahankara' (I have nothing to prove), we drop the immense weight of ego, unlocking genuine tranquility.
